concept.name: ML Pipeline Orchestration

relationships.description: Connects ML Pipeline Orchestration to llm prompt engineering in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Coordinate multi-stage data prep, distributed training, evaluation, and deployment as idempotent, lineage-tracked DAGs rather than fragile cron scripts.
spark.keyTakeaway: Separate control-plane orchestration from data-plane compute: pass immutable S3/GCS artifact URIs between tasks, never raw DataFrames, and decouple CPU preprocessing from GPU training.

concept.whyItMatters: Ad-hoc bash and cron scripts silently corrupt training runs when upstream schemas drift, waste $2–$4/hour per A100/H100 GPU waiting on CPU feature joins, and make reproducing a production model from 3 months ago impossible. Pipeline orchestration enforces deterministic retries, asset lineage, and automated quality gates.
whenToUse: Recurring training, fine-tuning, or batch inference workflows span 3+ dependent stages (ingestion, validation, feature engineering, training, evaluation).
Teams need automated backfills, failure recovery from mid-pipeline checkpoints, and strict audit lineage linking model weights to exact dataset snapshots.
Heterogeneous compute stages must run on different node pools (e.g., Spark/Ray CPU workers for ETL, 8xH100 nodes for training).
whenNotToUse: Single-step exploratory notebook experiments or one-off hyperparameter sweeps before a feature set stabilizes.
Sub-second real-time streaming inference or online feature updates better served by Flink, Kafka Streams, or Feast online stores.
Tiny datasets (<1 GB) that train in under 5 minutes on a single workstation without external data dependencies.
keyPoints: Model pipelines as Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) of idempotent, pure tasks keyed by logical execution date (`ds`) or dataset partition.
Pass lightweight metadata and immutable object-storage URIs (`s3://bucket/run_id/features.parquet`) between steps instead of serializing payloads through the orchestrator DB.
Insert automated data-validation gates (Great Expectations or Pandera) before GPU allocation to fail fast on null spikes or schema drift.
Decouple CPU-heavy tokenization/ETL from GPU training pods so expensive accelerators stay >85% utilized.
Gate model promotion on automated offline evaluation metrics (e.g., NDCG@10 or F1 delta >= +0.5% over production baseline) in MLflow or W&B.

examples.title: Dagster Asset Pipeline for Fraud Scoring
examples.scenario: A payments team ran 14 chained Airflow cron jobs where a 2-hour upstream Snowflake delay caused XGBoost training to silently run on yesterday's stale features.
examples.outcome: Migrating to Dagster software-defined assets with freshness policies and Pandera schema checks eliminated stale-data trains and cut weekly backfill time from 6 hours to 42 minutes.

examples.title: Decoupled Ray Data + Kubeflow Fine-Tuning
examples.scenario: An LLM fine-tuning job on 8xA100 GPUs spent 45% of its wall-clock time blocked on single-node Python JSONL tokenization.
examples.outcome: Splitting tokenization into a 32-CPU Ray Data preprocessing stage writing Parquet shards to S3 raised GPU SM utilization from 52% to 91% and saved $1,800/week.

tradeOffs.pro: Airflow has massive ecosystem operators for general ETL and SQL warehousing.
tradeOffs.con: Dagster and Kubeflow natively track dataset/model lineage and typed artifacts without custom XCom hacks.

tradeOffs.factor: Fine-Grained DAG Tasks vs. Coarse Monolithic Containers
tradeOffs.pro: Fine-grained tasks allow cheap retries of a failed evaluation step without re-running a 4-hour GPU train.
tradeOffs.con: Too many tiny tasks add 15–45 s Kubernetes pod-scheduling cold start per step.

tradeOffs.pro: Fixed schedules (daily/weekly) make GPU quota and cost forecasting predictable.
tradeOffs.con: Drift-triggered runs (e.g., PSI > 0.2) respond faster to distribution shifts but risk runaway retraining loops without cooldowns.

failureModes.name: Training-Serving Skew
failureModes.description: Offline pipeline SQL/Spark transformations diverge subtly from online Python/Go inference code, degrading production accuracy.
failureModes.mitigation: Compute shared definitions in a feature store (Feast/Tecton) or package identical transformation code into a versioned library.

failureModes.name: Orchestrator Metadata DB Bloat
failureModes.description: Passing DataFrames or numpy arrays via Airflow XComs saturates PostgreSQL and crashes the scheduler.
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce a strict <4 KB XCom limit and write all intermediate artifacts as Parquet/Safetensors to S3/GCS.

failureModes.name: Non-Idempotent Partial Backfills
failureModes.description: Retrying a failed task appends duplicate rows to a feature table, poisoning model weights.
failureModes.mitigation: Write outputs to partition-scoped paths (`dt=2026-11-12/`) using atomic overwrite or Iceberg/Delta Lake MERGE.

failureModes.name: Zombie GPU Allocations
failureModes.description: A training script hangs on a deadlocked NCCL all-reduce while Kubernetes keeps billing $32/hr for 8xH100s.

commonMistakes: Hardcoding `datetime.now()` inside pipeline tasks instead of using the orchestrator's logical execution timestamp.
Running data validation after model training instead of before provisioning GPU nodes.
Pinning `latest` Docker tags in pipeline specs, making historical runs impossible to reproduce.
Skipping automated champion-challenger evaluation gates before pushing weights to serving.
Triggering full-history recomputations on every run instead of incremental watermarked partitions.

sections.content:
## The idea

ML pipeline orchestration turns fragile, manual notebook sequences into **reproducible, observable Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs)** where each node is a containerized, idempotent step. Unlike traditional ETL, ML orchestration must coordinate heterogeneous hardware (CPU data clusters, multi-GPU training nodes, lightweight evaluation runners), track immutable data-to-weight lineage, and enforce statistical quality gates before any artifact reaches production.

## Concrete walkthrough

Consider a daily recommendation model retraining pipeline using **Kubeflow Pipelines / Argo Workflows** and **MLflow**:

1. **Partitioned Ingestion & Validation**: A Spark/Ray CPU job reads `s3://lake/events/dt={{ds}}/` and runs Pandera checks (row count > 1M, null rate < 0.5%). If validation fails, the DAG aborts in 90 seconds before touching GPUs.
2. **Feature Materialization**: Transformed features write to `s3://features/run_{{id}}/train.parquet` (using Apache Arrow zero-copy serialization) and log the dataset hash to MLflow.
3. **Checkpointed Distributed Training**: Argo schedules a PyTorch DDP pod on 4xA100 GPUs. The trainer reads Parquet shards, saves checkpoints every 15 minutes to S3, and tolerates spot-instance preemption via automatic resume.
4. **Evaluation & Registry Gate**: A CPU evaluation pod scores the candidate against a frozen golden holdout set. Only if `NDCG@10 >= baseline + 0.005` and `p99_latency <= 25ms` does it tag the model `Production` in MLflow.

sections.content:
## Lineage, idempotency, and reproducibility

Every production model must answer: *Which exact code commit, container digest, and dataset snapshot produced these weights?* Achieve this by:

- **Immutable Container Digests**: Reference images by SHA-256 (`model-train@sha256:9f8a...`), never mutable tags.
- **Deterministic Seeding & Partitioning**: Seed PRNGs (`torch.manual_seed`, `numpy.random.seed`) and bind data reads to Delta Lake / Apache Iceberg snapshot IDs so a retry 3 weeks later reads the identical rows.
- **Spot-Safe Checkpointing**: Persist optimizer state + epoch/step counter every 15 minutes so preempted GPU jobs resume with <15 minutes of lost work.

## Orchestration engines compared

| Engine | Primary Abstraction | Artifact Passing | K8s Native | Best Fit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Apache Airflow** | Imperative Task DAGs | XCom (metadata) + S3 hooks | Via KubernetesPodOperator | SQL/Spark ETL + light ML scheduling |
| **Dagster** | Software-Defined Assets | IO Managers (S3/Snowflake) | Yes (Helm/Daemon) | Data-centric ML with strict freshness & lineage |
| **Kubeflow / Argo** | Containerized Pipeline Steps | Native S3/GCS artifact paths | Yes (CRDs) | Heavy multi-GPU training & hyperparameter sweeps |
| **Metaflow** | Python `@step` decorators | Built-in S3 datastore | Yes (Argo/Batch export) | Rapid DS-to-prod iteration with minimal YAML |

## Failure modes

Orchestrated ML pipelines commonly degrade through **silent data issues and resource leaks**:

- **Silent Label Leakage**: Future-dated features slip into training snapshots when point-in-time joins (`ASOF JOIN`) are omitted, inflating offline AUC to 0.99 while failing online.
- **Pod Scheduling Thrash**: Launching 50 tiny 10-second Python tasks as separate Kubernetes pods wastes 30+ minutes in container pulls and scheduling overhead.
- **Stale Feature Store Sync**: Offline training finishes, but the online Redis/DynamoDB feature store backfill lags behind, serving zeros to the new model.

## Production hardening

Operate ML pipelines with the same rigor as tier-1 backend services:

- **Constrained Concurrency**: Set `max_active_runs=1` on backfill-enabled DAGs to prevent 10 parallel backfills from exhausting GPU quotas or saturating the warehouse.
- **Canary Shadowing**: Before full promotion, route 1–5% of live inference traffic to the newly promoted model in shadow mode and assert output distribution stability.
- **Cost Guardrails**: Tag every Kubernetes pod with `pipeline_id` and `run_id` and alert when single-run GPU spend exceeds 1.5x rolling median.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Pin all step containers by immutable SHA-256 digest and log Git commit + Iceberg/Delta snapshot ID.
- [ ] Enforce a fast CPU schema/null/drift validation gate before allocating any GPU nodes.
- [ ] Pass only S3/GCS URIs (<4 KB metadata) through the orchestrator; never pass raw datasets.
- [ ] Implement point-in-time (`ASOF`) joins to prevent label leakage between training and serving.
- [ ] Configure `activeDeadlineSeconds` and 15-minute S3 checkpoints on all GPU training steps.

interviewProblems.title: ML Pipeline Orchestration
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on ML Pipeline Orchestration. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Coordinate multi-stage data prep, distributed training, evaluation, and deployment as idempotent, lineage-tracked DAGs rather than fragile cron scripts.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: GPU Training Cluster applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Object Store & Registry.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Object Store & Registry experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Compute shared definitions in a feature store (Feast/Tecton) or package identical transformation code into a versioned library.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Separate control-plane orchestration from data-plane compute: pass immutable S3/GCS artifact URIs between tasks, never raw DataFrames, and decouple CPU preprocessing from GPU training.
Avoid trap: Hardcoding `datetime.now()` inside pipeline tasks instead of using the orchestrator's logical execution timestamp.
Avoid trap: Running data validation after model training instead of before provisioning GPU nodes.
When to reach for it: Recurring training, fine-tuning, or batch inference workflows span 3+ dependent stages (ingestion, validation, feature engineering, training, evaluation).
When to reach for it: Teams need automated backfills, failure recovery from mid-pipeline checkpoints, and strict audit lineage linking model weights to exact dataset snapshots.

putItTogether.title: Putting Ml Pipeline Orchestration Together
putItTogether.summary: Separate control-plane orchestration from data-plane compute: pass immutable S3/GCS artifact URIs between tasks, never raw DataFrames, and decouple CPU preprocessing from GPU training.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Ml Pipeline Orchestration before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Migrating to Dagster software-defined assets with freshness policies and Pandera schema checks eliminated stale-data trains and cut weekly backfill time from 6 hours to 42 minutes.
